reasoning: The extract shows a real commitment to evaluate, but not a full plan. Several lines say the Government will carry out a further review "before legislating to bring forward the rise in State Pension age to 68", which will consider "the latest life expectancy projections" and "evaluate the current rises in State Pension age". A timetable is given: the next review "will conclude by 2023" and the legislation provides for it "by July 2023". The extract also gives some reasons: the review will confirm when SPA rises to 68, allow "more recent life expectancy projections" and ensure "adequate notice". Success measures appear in the Fuller Working Lives lines: employment rate of over-50s by age band and gender, average age of exit from the labour market, and the employment rate gap between 50–64 and 35–49 year olds. The Government "will analyse the impact of changes... already in train" and "monitor the effects of State Pension age rises alongside the reforms". Together this reaches Level 2: measures, evaluation plans and a timetable. The strongest counter-example for Level 3 is that nothing says how the evaluation will be done, what outcomes would count as success or failure, or whether results will be published. Reference 42 only cites benefit expenditure tables and does not describe an evaluation. Nothing is said about testing the policy first or about consultation. To reach Level 3 the document would have to explain why this evaluation design was chosen, set out how and when results will be published, and say how they will feed into the decision.
